To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) studded eel passes have a complex flow field with a high degree of turbulence, (2) the flow field is sensitive to discharge, installation angle and tile spacing, (3) the swimming performance of juvenile eels is affected by the flow field, and (4) the swimming performance can be predicted with an individual-based model.
the passage efficiency of eel passes can be predicted by individual based models parametrized with flow field data derived from CFD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the movement of fish through a fish pass.
the movement and passage of juvenile eel through eel passes, and the design of such structures.
the design of eel passes, which are structures that enable elvers, juvenile eels to ascend barriers, such as dams, weirs and pumping plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

studded eel tile eel passes can be improved by using the following criteria: 1) a low installation angle of 5 degrees or lower; 2) a shallow slope of 2 degrees or lower; and 3) an elver size of 10 cm or larger.
this paper is the first to model the swimming of eel in a pass, and that it has been done with a very high level of detail.
the study provides a novel and comprehensive assessment of the performance of a novel type of fish pass for juvenile eels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the individual-based models are more accurate than cellular automata models, and that the individual based model can be used to predict elver passage through eel passes with reasonable accuracy.
the use of computational fluid dynamics to inform the design of eel passes can be a useful tool for practitioners.
the use of computational fluid dynamics to predict flow fields and the use of agent based models to predict elver movement can be used to inform the design and placement of eel passes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the installation angle of eel tiles should be set as shallow as possible to maximize passage efficiency.
the design of the substrate in eel passes can be improved to enhance passage efficiency.
the studded eel tile design can work well, but only when the slope is sufficiently low and the inflow discharge is sufficiently low.
